sentences.text: The Section 4 Notification was published on 09.10.2008 and the Land Acquisition Officer passed the Award on 01.02.2011.

Being not satisfied with the compensation determined by the SLAO @ Rs.1,44,250 per Hector, Rs.1,63,700/- per hector and Rs.1,80,000/- per Hector, the said Reference was preferred by the original claimant.
The necessary evidence was led by the claimant before the learned Reference court.
No evidence was led by the acquiring body.
By the impugned judgment and Award, the Reference came to be decided.
3) Heard the learned Advocate for the acquiring body, the learned Advocate for the claimant and the learned AGP for the State.
With their assistance, perused the papers on record.
a] It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Acquiring body that, in support of the claim for compensation for the land, the only evidence brought on record was that of the claimant.
The sale instances were brought on record.

As regards the trees are concerned, there is no entry of the six(6)
Kavita.
3/6 1-fa1021-17 Mango trees and Four (4) Char trees in the 7/12 extract.
The 7/12 extract do not show the well and pipe line.
The only evidence before the learned Reference Court was that of the valuer.
The learned reference court has erred in granting enhanced compensation in respect of the trees and the well and the pipe line.

b] It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the claimant that, the sale instances brought on record by the claimant are rightly considered by the learned Reference Court and proper compensation is awarded for the land.
The evidence of the valuer remained unshaken in the cross-examination.
The learned Reference Court has reduced the rate for the trees as evaluated by the valuer.
The learned Reference Court has rightly considered the reference on record.
Hence, no interference was called for in the impugned judgment and award.
c] It is submitted by the learned AGP that appropriate order be passed.
4) The learned Reference Court has decided bunch of reference applications by the common judgment and Award.
Undisputedly, the witnesses examined in all the reference applications are common.
In respect of the compensation towards the land, the learned Reference Court considered the sale instances brought on record at Exh.30 and 31.

The Kavita.
4/6 1-fa1021-17 observations in the judgment shows that, the sale instances were from same village and undisputedly, prior to the Section 4 Notification.
The learned Reference Court found the sale instance at Exh.31 as most relevant and determined the compensation for land @ Rs.7,73,807/- per hectare.
The learned Reference court considered the aspect of 10 % increase in value of the land.
The compensation in respect of the land is based on the material available on record in the nature of the aforesaid sale instances and supported with acceptable reasons.
Thus, no interference is called for in respect of the compensation determined for the land.
5) As regards the compensation for trees is concerned, undisputedly, the 7/12 extract refers to existence of Four hundred (400) Orange trees.

sentences.text: Mango trees and four (4) Char trees in 7/12 extract.

In support of the enhanced compensation,
towards the trees, the claimant examined the valuer and brought on record the valuation report.
The evidence shows that, the valuer visited the field.

Though cross examined by the acquiring body,
nothing has come on record so as to disbelieve the valuer that he visited the acquired land.

The valuer valued the trees as under:-
".......... for Amla trees @ Rs.9391/-, for Mango tree @ Rs.54106/-, for Char tree @
Rs.9394/-, for Lime tree @ Rs.4584/-, for Ber tree @ Rs.4752/-, for Orange tree @
Rs.8119/- and for Tamarind Kavita.

5/6 1-fa1021-17  tree @ Rs.10,280/-".
 6) The learned reference court considered the evidence of the valuer and reduced the rate valued by the valuer for the trees.
The tree was valued by the valuer at Rs.8119/- per tree and the learned reference court determined the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Orange tree.

For Mango trees, the valuer determined the rate of Rs.54106/- and the learned reference Court determined the rate of Rs. 30,000/-
per tree.
As regards the Char trees are concerned, the valuer valued the same at Rs.9394/- and the learned reference court determined the compensation for Rs.8,000/- per tree.
This clearly goes to show that, the learned reference Court did not accept the rate valued by the valuer as it is.
There is deduction in the rates valued by the valuer.
Therefore, there is no reason to interfere with the rate determined by the learned Reference court towards the trees.
7) As regards the compensation for well is concerned, the chart/statement of the Award passed by the SLAO do not show the well in the acquired land.
So also the 7/12 extract do not show the existence of well.
The valuers evidence show that, he found two (2) wells on the acquired land bearing gat no.129/2.
The valuation report by the valuer at Exh.34 is in detail with drawing/sketch of the well.
The said detailed report by the valuer, remained unshaken in the cross examination.
In the cross examination, it has come that he valued in all six (6) wells in his single visit.
The learned Reference Court has considered the report of the valuer and brought down the compensation for well with pipe line for Rs.3,00,000/-.
There is nothing to show as to why the evidence of the valuer should be discarded.
Thus, the Kavita.
6/6 1-fa1021-17 acceptance of the evidence of the valuer by the learned Reference court, in respect of the well needs no interference.
8) In view of the above discussion, it is clear that, the learned reference court passed the impugned judgment and award on the basis of the evidence on record.
